operator: National Air Cargo, dba National Airlines
operation_type: 14 CFR Part 121 supplemental commercial cargo flight
source_publisher: National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), United States
decision_reason: NTSB identifies N949CA as a Boeing 747-400 BCF, serial 25630, operated by National Air Cargo/National Airlines on a Part 121 supplemental cargo flight; all seven crewmembers died.

reconciliation_evidence.observation: IATA Annex 3 lists National Airlines Boeing 747 at Bagram as a cargo Western-jet hull loss after takeoff.

reconciliation_evidence.record: 2013 Statistical Summary / National Air Cargo Group 747-400
reconciliation_evidence.observation: Boeing's worldwide commercial-jet table lists National Air Cargo Group 747-400 as scheduled cargo, destroyed, fatal, 7/7.

operation_type: regularly scheduled international passenger flight / 14 CFR Part 129
location: San Francisco International Airport, California, United States
source_publisher: National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), United States
decision_reason: NTSB identifies Asiana flight 214 as Boeing 777-200ER HL7742, serial 29171, on a regularly scheduled international passenger flight; three passengers were fatally injured.

reconciliation_evidence.observation: IATA Annex 3 lists the Asiana Boeing 777 passenger Western-jet hull loss at San Francisco.
Boeing's worldwide commercial-jet statistics identify Asiana 777-200 as a fatal 2013 scheduled-passenger accident.

source_publisher: Interstate Aviation Committee (IAC/MAK), Air Accident Investigation Commission
decision_reason: IAC/MAK identifies Boeing 737-500 VQ-BBN, operated by Tatarstan Airlines, as commercial air transport; all 44 passengers and six crew died and the aircraft was destroyed.

reconciliation_evidence.observation: IATA Annex 3 lists Tatarstan Boeing 737 as a passenger Western-jet hull loss after loss of control during go-around.

reconciliation_evidence.record: 2013 Year in Review / Commercial Jets Major Accidents
reconciliation_evidence.observation: Independent commercial-jet review lists Tatarstan B737 at Kazan with 50 fatalities.
